subject: mathematics
question_text: If f(x) = 2x − 1 and g(x) = x², find (fg)(x).

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.11, chapter 2 FUNCTIONS, Very Short Answer question 16(ii). Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1 split rewards writing the product f(x)·g(x) first and the expanded form with its domain second. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A runs Q1–Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find (fg)(x) — what fg means, the expanded form, and the domain.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Multiply the two outputs
steps.margin_note: First mark. (fg)(x) is a product of VALUES, not a composition: f(x) times g(x) at the same x.
lines: f(x) = 2x − 1 and g(x) = x², both on R

recall.must_convey: That (fg)(x) = f(x)·g(x) = (2x − 1)x², a product of values and not a composition.
accept: f g of x is f of x times g of x
multiply two x minus one by x squared
it is a product of the two values not a composition
write f of x into g of x

steps.why: fg and fog are different operations. fg multiplies the two outputs at the same x; fog puts one output inside the other. This line shows which one was used.
steps.memory_tip: fg means multiply, fog means substitute. There is no small circle in fg.
common_mistakes: Adding the outputs instead of multiplying them.

steps.label: Expand and state the domain
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Multiply x² into each term of the bracket, and say the domain is R because both parts are polynomials.
lines: f and g are defined for every real x,

recall.must_convey: That the product expands to 2x³ − x² and the domain is R.
accept: two x into x squared is two x cubed and one into x squared is x squared
the answer is two x cubed minus x squared
the domain is all real numbers because both are polynomials
multiply through and get two x cubed minus x squared

steps.why: Multiplying a bracket by x² adds 2 to the power of each term inside it. The domain of a product is where both functions are defined, and two polynomials are defined everywhere.
steps.memory_tip: Multiplying by x² adds 2 to every power: 2x becomes 2x³, and 1 becomes x².
common_mistakes: Writing 2x³ − 1 by multiplying x² into the first term only.
Leaving the answer without saying the domain is R.
